gitShaNote: THE RELEASE SHA. The §289 artifact commit, which adds this preservation package, the controlled-production deployment sequence, the operations corrections and the §289 evidence. It is COMMITTED LOCALLY AND NOT PUSHED; see deployment.pushState.

sourceDigest.value: MOVES WITH EACH DOCUMENTATION COMMIT — not a release binding
sourceDigest.definition: sha256 over the LC_ALL=C-sorted lines of `git ls-tree -r <sha> --format='%(path) %(objectname)'`, covering every tracked file.
sourceDigest.why: Recorded for completeness and deliberately NOT used as the release binding. It covers documentation and evidence, so it changes on every §289 artifact commit including the one that would record it. applicationSourceDigest is the release binding.

applicationSourceDigest.recompute: git ls-tree -r HEAD --format='%(path) %(objectname)' | grep -E '^(backend/(src|scripts)/|backend/package(-lock)?\.json|backend/tsconfig|frontend-next/(app|components|lib|public|scripts)/|frontend-next/package(-lock)?\.json|frontend-next/(next\.config|tsconfig|tailwind))' | LC_ALL=C sort | shasum -a 256
applicationSourceDigest.definition: The same construction restricted to the files that determine the BUILT ARTIFACTS.
applicationSourceDigest.why: THE RELEASE BINDING. It changes only when the deployable product changes, so it is stable across the documentation commits that a preservation package necessarily adds.

retiredDigestMustNotBeUsed.why: Misattributed historical digest, retired at §288 (register entry PV-2). It is recorded here ONLY so a future reader who encounters it knows it is retired rather than reusing it as an integrity assertion.

deployment.commitsAheadOfDeployedProduction: at least 53 and growing with each §289 artifact commit; the count is not a release binding

knownLimitations.PV-NODE-UNPINNED: No Node version is pinned in either package and the Render runtime version could not be read. A rebuild reproduces the source digest but not, provably, the artifact.
knownLimitations.OPS-DB-PROVIDER-MISSTATED: Two operations documents name Render as the database platform; production is Neon. An operator following deployment-runbook step 3 would look for a Render Postgres instance that does not exist.
knownLimitations.DB-4-OUTCOMES-TABLE-PRESENT: The `outcomes` table EXISTS in production (13 columns, 0 rows) although no migration creates it. The containment argument recorded in the code and in register entry DB-3 — that the cross-tenant recurrence check is unreachable because the table is absent — does not hold in production.
knownLimitations.EXPERT-DISABLED: EXPERT_EXECUTION_ENABLED=false in production. Live provider transport has never been exercised; hazlenz:verify reports UNVERIFIED_LIVE for provider transport.
knownLimitations.STORAGE-REPORT-ROUNDTRIP-NOT-DONE: Production object storage is verified at the infrastructure level (§269 and again at §289) but no generated report has ever been round-tripped through it via the product route.
knownLimitations.NO-MONITORING-AGGREGATION: Operational events are emitted to stdout/stderr with redaction. There is no aggregation, alerting or error tracking (register MO-1).
knownLimitations.NEON-RETENTION-UNREAD: Neon's control plane was not reachable from this session (no NEON_* credential). The platform backup retention window and point-in-time-recovery setting are UNREAD. The operator-controlled logical backup path is proven independently.
knownLimitations.LEGAL-NOT-CLEARED: Terms, Privacy Notice, third-party model disclosure, contracting entity and trademark clearance are all open at Threshold C. Nothing here asserts legal clearance.
knownLimitations.NO-EXTERNAL-BETA: External beta remains BLOCKED regardless of Threshold A status.

validationEvidence.section289: verification/current/threshold-a-289/ — this section's production reads, backup, restore rehearsal, migration rehearsal and gate results

productSourceCommit.why: THE STABLE IDENTITY. The §289 release build and the full gate set ran against this commit, and it does not move.
productSourceCommit.equivalence: Every §289 commit after this one touches only project-docs/ and verification/ and changes no backend or frontend source, so applicationSourceDigest is unchanged and the gate results obtained here bind whatever tip is deployed.
productSourceCommit.recompute: git ls-tree -r HEAD --format='%(path) %(objectname)' | grep -E '^(backend/(src|scripts)/|backend/package(-lock)?\.json|backend/tsconfig|frontend-next/(app|components|lib|public|scripts)/|frontend-next/package(-lock)?\.json|frontend-next/(next\.config|tsconfig|tailwind))' | LC_ALL=C sort | shasum -a 256

releaseSha.binding: The release SHA is the branch tip at push time and CANNOT be recorded inside the commit that would record it — each such commit changes the value. So the release is bound by a digest instead of by a SHA, which is the stronger binding in any case: the SHA to deploy is whatever origin/beta/expert-hazlenz-validated-candidate-2026-09-12 points at after step 1, PROVIDED its applicationSourceDigest equals 2ce8a1d7b045818cb9708af9414fe8d189523e334dad955b617268cc932f2618. Verify that before deploying; it is one command.
releaseSha.verify: git ls-tree -r HEAD --format='%(path) %(objectname)' | grep -E '^(backend/(src|scripts)/|backend/package(-lock)?\.json|backend/tsconfig|frontend-next/(app|components|lib|public|scripts)/|frontend-next/package(-lock)?\.json|frontend-next/(next\.config|tsconfig|tailwind))' | LC_ALL=C sort | shasum -a 256
